speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; how long has this wound been present, and have you noticed any recent changes in its size or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your family history and prior DVT, could you describe the appearance of your leg swelling and the wound itself? Are the veins visible or does the skin feel warm? Also, do you experience pain, itching, or any drainage from the wound?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stasis Dermatitis with Secondary Infection (likely due to Chronic Venous Insufficiency).

*Note: While you mentioned a previous suggestion of "Pyelonephritis," that condition affects the kidneys and would not present as a chronic lower leg wound with a family history of venous issues. Your symptoms strongly indicate a circulatory problem. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Wound_Photo_Right_Lower_Leg*
